key_insight: Long-horizon agents fail when important context fades from the active window, so memory should not just retrieve information passively—it should proactively surface what matters right before it is needed. This paper reframes memory as an active control mechanism to prevent "behavioral state decay".
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of long-horizon decision-making where task requirements, environment facts, prior attempts, diagnoses, and open subgoals become buried in long trajectories or fall outside the context window, causing agents to make poor decisions.
method: Introduces a proactive memory agent that actively intervenes to bring decision-relevant state back into focus.
Treats memory as an action-oriented system rather than a passive retrieval store.
Targets key information that is most likely to affect the next decision in long-horizon trajectories.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical way to improve agent reliability on long tasks without relying only on larger context windows. It can help agents stay aligned with goals, avoid repeated mistakes, and use past experience more effectively.

paper_title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
paper_authors: Yifan Wu, Lizhu Zhang, Yuhang Zhou, Mingyi Wang, Bo Peng
